title: Claim Acceptance, Documents and Payment Timing
content:
# Claim Acceptance, Documents and Payment Timing — Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda

This chapter of the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda claims manual sets when a claim is accepted and when its benefit is paid. Every condition is decided on the system records of the waiver and of the claim line, never on the holder's statement alone.

## Conditions of payment

1. **Waiver status.** A GAP balance benefit is paid only on a waiver in active status, and a replacement vehicle credit only on a waiver in claim settled status. The status read is that of the same waiver the claim is made under.
2. **Covered loss.** Only a total loss is covered where the waiver leaves out partial losses; a vehicle declared a loss for mechanical breakdown is excluded where the waiver excludes it; and where the waiver requires primary insurance there must be a primary physical-damage insurance total-loss settlement.
3. **Notice.** A claim is accepted only when it is reported within the waiver's claim notice period, in calendar days after the primary insurer's settlement date recorded for that claim number.
4. **Documents.** The required documents (settlement letter, payoff letter, payment history, the installment contract) must arrive within the waiver's documents period, in calendar days after the claim is reported.
5. **Payment.** An approved benefit is paid within the waiver's claim payment period after the last document.
6. **Theft.** A theft claim is paid only after the vehicle has stayed unrecovered for the waiver's theft waiting period, in calendar days after the loss date.
7. **Denial and review.** A denied line names its denial reason. The holder may submit new evidence within the waiver's denial appeal period, in calendar days after the denial, and a review that overturns the denial pays the line as a new paid benefit entry.

## Counting the notice period

Calendar days are added to the settlement date, which is day 0; the last day of the period is the settlement date plus the notice period, and a report on the last day is in time. The comparison is "not later than": a report on or before the last day meets the condition, a report after it does not.

| Hypothetical case (notice period of 90 days) | Settlement date | Reported on | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Report on the boundary day | Day 0 | Day 90 | yes |
| Report the day after the boundary | Day 0 | Day 91 | no |
| Report the day before the boundary | Day 0 | Day 89 | yes |

## Points of judgement

- The settlement date is the one recorded on the claim line for that claim number; a date the holder recalls does not replace it.
- A waiver already in claim settled status takes no further GAP balance benefit; the only line it may still carry is a replacement vehicle credit.
